title: Dipole chains of Bloch point singularities revealed by X-ray magnetic tomography
authors: Jeffrey Neethirajan, Rikako Yamamoto, Marisel Di Pietro Martínez, Luke A. Turnbull, Praveen Vir, Chandra Shekar, Claudia Felser, Luis Carlos Colocho Hurtarte, Benedikt J. Daurer, Majid Kazemian, Burkhard Kaulich, Claire Donnelly
abstract: Bloch point singularities play an important role in magnetic systems, mediating changes in topology in three dimensional configurations. However, until now they have only been observed as isolated objects or as part of individual topological textures. Here we present the experimental observation of a 1D dipole chain of Bloch points in an anisotropic chiral magnet using soft X-ray magnetic vector tomography. We identify that the chain of Bloch point singularities lies along a boundary between regions of opposite chirality and that neighbouring Bloch and anti-Bloch points are stable at separations down to 60 nm. The stability of the Bloch points is determined to be closely related to the surrounding topology of the magnetisation configuration and a threshold separation for the spontaneous annihilation of Bloch point-anti-Bloch point pairs within chiral domain walls is identified to be approximately 90 nm in distance. This observation of a chain of Bloch points and the insight into their stability, offers a route to explore the correlative behaviour of such topological point defects. The behaviour and control of such point defects is of relevance for the control of 3D magnetisation configurations, and provides a new route towards the creation of correlated configurations of singularities in a magnetic system.
summary: This work reports the first experimental observation of a one-dimensional chain of Bloch point singularities in a chiral magnet using soft X-ray magnetic tomography. By mapping the 3D magnetization, the researchers quantified the stability of these topological defects, finding that they persist over significant distances and identifying a critical separation for their spontaneous annihilation.
main_problem: To experimentally observe and study the collective behavior of Bloch point singularities in a 3D magnetic system, moving beyond observations of isolated or simple topological textures.
main_result: The authors observed a 1D dipole chain of Bloch point singularities in a chiral magnet, finding that neighboring Bloch and anti-Bloch points are stable down to 60 nm, with an annihilation threshold near 90 nm.
method: Soft X-ray ptychographic magnetic vector tomography, utilizing X-ray Magnetic Circular Dichroism (XMCD) to reconstruct the 3D magnetization configuration.
model_or_system: The study uses an anisotropic chiral magnet, specifically a Heusler alloy ($	ext{Mn}_{1.4}	ext{PtSn}$), fabricated into a wedge-shaped lamella to create a continuous thickness gradient.
key_observables: Bloch point singularities, magnetic chirality (clockwise/counterclockwise winding), domain wall structure, and the 3D magnetization vector components ($M_x, M_y, M_z$).
important_parameters: Separation stability down to 60 nm; annihilation threshold of $\approx 90$ nm; sample thickness gradient from 170 nm to 500 nm.
main_assumptions: The technique overcomes previous limitations by probing 3D configurations in samples up to 500 nm thick, and the analysis assumes the weak stray magnetic field does not alter the magnetic state between measurements.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the thickness-dependent domain size, 2D stripe domain patterns, and 3D reconstructions showing the location and stability of Bloch point chains along domain boundaries.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the need to study collective defects to presenting the experimental setup (tomography), detailing the observation of the 1D dipole chain, and quantifying the stability limits of these topological point defects.
why_interesting: While focused on magnetism, the study of topological defects and their stability thresholds (like the 90 nm annihilation distance) provides a physical model for understanding defect-mediated phase transitions or energy barriers in complex many-body systems, which has analogies in quantum materials.
